title: Guidelines for providers of general-purpose AI models

evidence.quote: providers should review their obligations, assess model risks, prepare for compliance
providers of the most advanced models, i.e. those that pose systemic risks, are legally obliged to notify the AI Office of these models
Reports of serious incident pursuant to Art 55(1)(c) of the AI Act
Safety and Security Framework and Model Report pursuant to Measures 1.4 and 7.7 of the Safety and Security Chapter of the GPAI Code of Practice
Notifications of a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk pursuant to Art 51(2) and 52(2) of the AI Act
Reports on how providers of general-purpose AI models who have not signed the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice intend to comply with the AI Act
The Commission will enforce compliance with the obligations for providers of GPAI models, including with fines
The AI Office will support providers in their compliance, especially Code of Practice signatories
Providers of general-purpose AI models must use the EU SEND platform to submit documents related to their obligations to the AI Office

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Guidelines are explicitly stated as 'not legally binding' but reflect the Commission's interpretation and will guide enforcement. Enforcement powers (including fines) enter into application 2 August 2026. Providers of models placed on market before 2 August 2025 have until 2 August 2027 to comply. The GPAI Code of Practice is a complementary voluntary tool.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance as enabling confident innovation through clarity and pragmatic obligations. Repeated emphasis on helping actors 'innovate with confidence,' exemptions for open-source to 'promote transparency and innovation,' and the stated EU approach of promoting 'excellence and trust' while boosting 'research and industrial capacity' signals an innovation-enablement framing. Safety and fundamental rights appear as secondary justifications.

evidence_spans.quote: help actors in the AI ecosystem understand whether the obligations apply to them and what is expected of them, ensuring they can innovate with confidence
The guidelines for providers of GPAI model help stakeholders across the AI value chain innovate with clarity and confidence
The EU's approach to artificial intelligence promotes excellence and trust, by boosting research and industrial capacity while ensuring safety and fundamental rights
clarify under what conditions providers of open-source AI models are exempt from certain obligations, to promote transparency and innovation
